PAPER.TITLE: Digital Advertising Auctions with Asymmetric Consumer Information
PAPER.PLAINTEXT: This paper studies how unequal access to consumer information changes bidding competition in digital advertising auctions.

ABSTRACT.P: We study how asymmetric access to consumer data shapes competition in real-time bidding advertising markets.

SECTION.title: Model
SECTION.P: Two platforms bid for one advertising impression. The integrated platform is informed with probability \alpha.
SECTION.PROPOSITION: Greater access to data softens competition and raises both bidders' expected payoff.
SECTION.P: This result follows from the equilibrium bidding distributions.The full proof appears in the appendix.

SECTION.title: Conclusion
SECTION.P: Consumers benefit from improved targeting, while the integrated platform may prefer to preserve a closed data ecosystem.
